topics.title: Continental drift theory and its driving forces

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Wegener's continental drift theory, Pangaea, Panthalassa and the split into Laurasia and Gondwanaland.
Explain the pole-fleeing and tidal forces proposed by Wegener and why they were rejected.

topics.title: Evidence in support of continental drift
topics.ncert_sections: Evidence in Support of the Continental Drift

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the jig-saw fit of coastlines and rocks of the same age across oceans support drift.
Interpret tillite, placer deposits and fossil distribution as evidence of continental drift.

topics.title: Post-drift studies and the ocean floor
topics.ncert_sections: Post-drift Studies; Convectional Current Theory; Mapping of the Ocean Floor; Ocean Floor Configuration; Distribution of Earthquakes and Volcanoes

concepts.learning_objective: Explain Arthur Holmes's convection current theory and its role in answering the problem of force.
Identify the divisions of the ocean floor: continental margins, abyssal plains and mid-oceanic ridges.
Interpret the global distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes and their focal depths.
Recall the facts about ocean-floor rocks, sediments and magnetism revealed by post-drift studies.
Explain Hess's hypothesis of sea floor spreading and the consumption of crust at trenches.

topics.title: Plate tectonics and plate boundaries
topics.ncert_sections: Plate Tectonics; Divergent, Convergent and Transform Boundaries

concepts.learning_objective: Define a tectonic plate and identify the major and minor plates of the world.
Distinguish divergent, convergent and transform plate boundaries with examples.

topics.title: Rate of plate movement and its driving force
topics.ncert_sections: Rates of Plate Movement; Force for the Plate Movement

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how magnetic stripes give the rates of plate movement and compare slow and fast ridges.
Explain convection cells in the mantle as the force behind plate movement.
Identify the northern, eastern, western and southern boundaries of the Indian plate.
Describe India's northward journey, the Deccan Traps and the formation of the Himalayas.
